quest.title: Peace to the Slumbering
quest.description: The Greater Shadow Pin falls, opening a huge hole in the ground...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x2

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Why's there a stone tablet here?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: It might have been left by tribesfolk of the past. That happens quite often around here. Long ago, this was a boundary marker, telling you that "you've crossed the line!"

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: You can sometimes find stones with patterns carved in white on them throughout our lands that serve the same purpose. They've just all been abandoned.

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what's happened.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Boundaries and borders are no laughing matter here... Between the living and the dead, within and without, above and below... Only those who have crossed these lines can grasp the dangers they face.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: It is said that there was once a stone tablet in an ancient ruin that read thus: "If any tread past this stone with ill-intent, mine hand shall drake-claw become, and grasp their neck shall I."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err, wait. What if this stone tablet has some sort of warning or curse on it, then?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: I can tell at a glance... Traore left this here. To think that... *sigh*

choices.text: Wait, where have I heard that name...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's from the story you told us before, right, Titu? When the Abyss was corrupting Natlan, he led the tribesfolk against them... and against two soldiers from Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Haha, you're quite the avid listeners. Storytellers love people like you, y'know?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: After all, the capacity to remember such tales is a basic quality that all storytellers must have.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Let me see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It says, friends from afar... "Zephaniah and Irizar."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... "You would prefer to be known as cowards, rogues, or a thorn in our side — that you should ever increase our vigilance, like an aphid that bites a Saurian."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Yet I must speak the truth here. Forever and always shall you be heroes who fought alongside our tribe, the brother-kin of the Children of Echoes."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, wait, so those Khaenri'ahns fought alongside the tribe, then?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Well... The names of those two have always featured in stories as the embodiment... of evil. They've even appeared in my nightmares.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: "If you don't stop crying, the ghosts of the Khaenri'ahn soldiers will follow the sound and track down your shadow..." So they said. But... it was all a lie?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Such injustice... that those who gave their all for our tribe should bear such slander.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's... so sad.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Oroo...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They did not care for their good name...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They only wished to see their will fulfilled.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how it is... Paimon gets it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Most heroes don't do great deeds to become heroes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They become heroes because they do those deeds. That's why they don't care about what others think of them...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *sigh* Perhaps you're right, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, there the Iridescent Inscription goes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wow, so this... This must've been where they finally sealed the Abyss. Look, {NICKNAME}, there are so many golden patterns in the middle there...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can also see traces of Abyss leakage here.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Looks like that's the thing attracting the Iridescent Inscription. We need to get over there and have a look...

choices.text: Ah, that's the elder who fought against the Abyss...

dialogues.text: *hiss* Ugh— Aaah— I told you— It's dangerous, g—get out of here—
Calamity— the seal— torn apart—

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Hroo... Rowrr...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: That voice is more complete now, but... Somehow, it's not as frightening as before.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: My head still hurts a little, though.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #How you feeling, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's good...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Anyway! How are you feeling, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Mmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, looks like you're fine, too.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Now that we're here, it's clear that the voices we heard coming from the stone pillar must've been...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Those of the Khaenri'ahn soldiers who've been sealed here too...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rrooh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means they were sealed in for many years, alongside the Abyss... But what's gone wrong here?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I think... The problem here is similar to the one we encountered with the Lesser Shadow Pins above. The surging Abyss has caused the Iridescent Inscription's power to shatter and be squeezed out of that giant sealing pillar...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means we'll need to find the large Inscription's fragments and find a way to put this "eggshell" back together again, right?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Indeed. That way, the seal can be fully restored, and the Abyss will stay sealed in this place. Then... Everything will likely go back to normal.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But as with the Lesser Shadow Pins, the solid phlogiston surface will have an intense adversarial reaction to the Abyss, which is why the ground undulates so...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: We must be careful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where are we gonna find said fragments, though?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr... Rawr!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh? Can you sense the Inscription's power hidden inside that thing, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}? You sure do have a pretty sharp nose... Wait, you were using your nose, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, was that stone even there before?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #Did it... just appear as you approached the large Inscription, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, whatever. Let's take a look around that rock first, shall we?

choices.text: Now that's what they call "surround sound."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? That's not what Paimon was asking at all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, this is weird. There was all that scattered light earlier... and then we suddenly found ourselves here...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. That's...

dialogues.speaker: "Beast With Fur Like That of Night"
dialogues.text: Come... over here...

dialogues.speaker: "Beast With Fur Like That of Night"
dialogues.text: You have brought so many slumberers, they who should have rested in peace...

dialogues.speaker: "Beast With Fur Like That of Night"
dialogues.text: Perhaps they prayed to spirits they should not have beseeched...

dialogues.speaker: "Beast With Fur Like That of Night"
dialogues.text: But that was a moonless night, where naught could be seen. The Night has long forgiven them. Yet hate and filth shall never rest, and they too shall never truly sleep again.

dialogues.speaker: "Beast With Fur Like That of Night"
dialogues.text: Thank you, O you who are beloved... You have soothed their fury, which raged in the darkness. It was you who brought them into the Night's reflection. The outland souls, too, may now return where they were headed...

dialogues.speaker: "Beast With Fur Like That of Night"
"Beast With Fur Like That of Night"
dialogues.text: Go now. But beware the fearful instigators, and the ends plotted by those bearing ill-intent.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: #Hah... What do you think, {NICKNAME}. Shall we unseal the Iridescent Inscription now?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Then I'll get to it... But please, be very careful.

choices.text: Give me a moment more to prepare.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: No worries. Just tell me once you're done...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Just touch it once more and let the power of the phlogiston flow fully through the Inscription. That way, the "eggshell" should seal up completely... preventing the Abyss from escaping.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that should solve our problem...

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Hmm... Let me try...
Quick, quick! Seal us inside too— Just as we agreed—
*hiss*— Then leave. Get out of here— Why aren't you leaving— The calamity—

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Listen! There are more voices — more than those two soldiers, for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
Behind the glowing inscriptions, from a place further still than the anguished howls...
You hear wrathful roars, and the pained whimpering of Saurians.
You hear the sound of inchoate flesh and blood merging, the sick, giant, sticky, approaching footfalls of some giant thing beyond description.
But you also hear something like thousands of hands, thousands constantly resisting, pushing outward...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You hear the endless battle in the narrow darkness.\nIt is... torment unto eternity.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Those heroes are still locked in battle to this day, preventing the Abyss from flooding out from the Iridescent Inscription.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: The stories I tell have purpose. We must always remember those brave warriors and their sacrifices.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And yet... Such suffering. "Though the heroes were wounded, they shook it off, and stood up, nothing hurt withal." That is what the stories say.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: But real wounds cannot be so easily shaken, nor true torment so easily conquered... There they have suffered so long, in that tiny, lightless world.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Hroo!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't there... anything we can do for them?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I want to as well, but the Abyss...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Perhaps the only thing we can do is inherit their will and reseal the Inscription. Nor has this been the first time the Shadow Pin has fallen — in our tribe's tales, anyway.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Someone must have been here before, and someone must have read Traore's tablet. Those who came before to restore the Inscription must have seen what we saw.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And yet... Our stories did not change, for the warnings they gave were real, as were the dangers.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: All we can do is restore the Inscription and leave. To remember always, and never forget all that we have witnessed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still... Ugh. They're supposed to be heroes! But they've been left here to suffer forever...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're right, Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This is no end for heroes.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I know that. I wish to give them peace, too. But I don't have that power. I'm just... a storyteller.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rrooh!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #...Really? You'd do that, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Of course {M#he}{F#she} would. Cross Paimon's heart!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: The Abyss is dangerous beyond compare... I'm not questioning your strength, but don't push yourself too hard.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry. We've got experience with stuff like this — and we have the Inscription in a pinch, too.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: True...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *sigh* You're even more impressive than I could have imagined. To be willing to give your all to resolve others' pain... Truly, you are great heroes.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #And I am a storyteller... so I will record the tales of heroes. Well then, {NICKNAME}, O hero from another land, please... Show me how you shall valiantly triumph over the Abyss.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That we shall do.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: So... Shall we unseal the Iridescent Inscription now, or do you want to make some preparations first?

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #Alright. I wish you success, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: One moment. Let's prep real quick.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #Sure. Do all you need to... and be careful, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: "Irizar"
dialogues.text: "Leave! Go... I don't want him to see me— like this—"

dialogues.speaker: "Irizar"
dialogues.text: (The voice seems to come from the very depths of the unmoving statue. There is a hint of respect toward someone remaining within...)

dialogues.speaker: Yukom
dialogues.text: Uh, are you guys alright? What happened just now?

dialogues.speaker: Yukom
dialogues.text: There was this sudden, massive earthquake! I was pretty worried, honestly, but it's good that you're alright.

dialogues.speaker: Yukom
dialogues.text: As for Titu... Why hasn't that guy come to take over this post yet? Ugh. I'd rather the earthquake flattened me at this point!

talks.objective: Listen to the whispers of Night

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: #You're back! {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]} and I were worried, honestly.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: But hah, what did I say, little fella? They're fine, see?

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Oooroo...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh. Not that we could explain where we went just now...

choices.text: It's a long story for sure...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #In any case, thank you, {NICKNAME}. I never expected that the Abyss here could truly be purified.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: The Iridescent Inscription, too, is gone — almost as if it no longer needed to stay. The tormented voices have also fallen silent.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And that golden light! How it flowed like water, spreading across the ground.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I even felt as if there were people within that light, waving at us...

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Did you see them too, little one? And there was that light that surrounded you — and then you were gone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. We didn't see anything, though...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #*sigh* Thank you so much once again, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. You too, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: You truly are remarkable heroes. Thank you, on behalf of all those warriors who can finally know peace. Traore's final wishes have been fulfilled, and...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: As for those two Khaenri'ahn soldiers— no, Khaenri'ahn heroes! Now that the Abyss is no longer present, they need no longer serve as a warning to us.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I must pen a story about them, about how they helped save the Children of Echoes... In truth, I did have a flash of revelation as to what their thoughts must've been.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: The Abyss represents such terrible peril that, were it up to me, I too might have made up some horror story to keep others from the tribe clear of this place.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: *sigh* It seems almost funny how I was previously worried about having nothing to write. Now there's almost too much here — in our tale about a golden-haired outlander, a flying white fairy, a little Tepetlisaurus, and how they saved our tribe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that sounds like a pretty awesome synopsis already!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Indeed. Stories pass on and stories change. Perhaps one day, a long, long time hence, even you might become as big as a mountain, Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Haargh! Behold, the mighty mountain, Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! Look ye, how she swallows a Sweet Madame the size of a Sumpter Beast in a single bite!

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr! Rawr!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Haha, I doubt there'd be too many of those, Paimon.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: And as these stories pass down... I imagine that those two soldiers, too, will eventually become heroes. They might not have cared themselves, but I know that this is what I must do.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: #Once again, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you have my utmost thanks... You too, of course, sharp little {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.

response.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
response.text: Rawr!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: As a storyteller, I swear to write for you the most exciting tale of adventure!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: Speaking of that— Oh, I should probably... head back to the sentry post to take up my shift.

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I'd almost forgotten about that amidst all the excitement...

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: ...Ugh. I sure hope Yukom doesn't tear me a new one for being gone so long!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, uh, you should totally get back there pronto!

response.speaker: Titu
response.text: I—I see...

dialogues.speaker: "Zephaniah"
dialogues.text: "Leave... Seal this place— as promised—"

dialogues.speaker: "Zephaniah"
dialogues.text: (That voice seems to come from the very depths of the unmoving statue. The rejection in those words are like two resolute hands that aim to push you from this place...)
Come... over here...
You have brought so many slumberers, they who should have rested in peace...
